name: Color Channel Independence Analysis
description: Evaluates the statistical decorrelation and independence between RGB color channels. Physical cameras capture light across overlapping spectral bands (via Bayer filters), resulting in a natural cross-channel correlation. Generative AI models often synthesize color channels with mathematically anomalous independence or physically impossible channel dependencies.
algorithm: Inter-channel Spectral Correlation & Mutual Information Modeling
mechanism: The algorithm isolates the RGB and YCbCr channels to compute their mutual information, Pearson correlation coefficients, and high-frequency structural dependencies. In an authentic photograph, the physical properties of the camera's color filter array dictate a highly predictable spectrum of inter-channel correlation. Generative AI models, which predict pixel values natively from latent space distributions rather than simulating a physical sensor grid, often fail to perfectly replicate these subtle organic interactions. This results in localized color bleeding, impossible hue gradients, or unnatural statistical independence where strong correlation should biologically exist.
parameters: Color Space: RGB/YCbCr, Metrics: Pearson Correlation Matrix, Mutual Information, Window Size: Global/Block-based
accuracy: Moderate to High (75-85%) - Consistently effective against older GANs and helpful in detecting diffusion model artifacts when combined with structural checks.
source: Farid (2009) / McCloskey & Albright (2018) - Color Cues in Forensics
useCase: Detecting AI generation through abnormal color synthesis, identifying localized color manipulation, and verifying the physical spectral response of the supposed capturing device.

references.title: Farid, H. (2009). Image Forgery Detection. IEEE Signal Processing Magazine.
McCloskey, S. & Albright, M. (2018). Detecting GAN-generated Imagery using Color Cues. IEEE WACV.

strengths:
• Anchored in the fundamental physics of camera sensors rather than relying on high-level semantic pixel geometry.
• Computationally lightweight, utilizing fast linear algebra matrices to process the entire image rapidly.
• Fundamentally difficult for current generative models to optimize without baking in restrictive, dedicated spectral physics constraints.
• Highly effective at spotting localized image splicing/Photoshop, where the color correlation matrix is suddenly mismatched.
limitations:
• Heavy post-production manual color grading, stylized cinematic LUTs, or extreme HDR merging can severely alter baseline channel dependencies, causing false positive alerts.
• Standard format compression (especially JPEG 4:2:0 chroma subsampling) permanently destroys critical high-frequency channel correlations.
• Utterly ineffective on grayscale, sepia, or natively monochrome images.
• Sometimes struggles on pure flat-color graphic design areas, CGI skies, or cartoon backgrounds lacking natural light gradients.
